did_you_know.text: Ahaz king of Judah began to reign in the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel.
Ahaz reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years, and Scripture notes that he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
Ahaz followed the ways of the kings of Israel and even sacrificed his son in the fire, a practice Scripture describes as an abomination of the nations.
Rezin king of Aram and Pekah king of Israel went up to fight against Jerusalem and besieged it, but they were unable to capture it.
Instead of relying on his own strength against Aram and Israel, Ahaz appealed to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria and asked him to save him.
To bribe the king of Assyria, Ahaz took silver and gold from the temple of the LORD and from the royal treasuries and sent them to him.
The king of Assyria granted Ahaz’s request, captured Damascus, deported its inhabitants to Kir, and put Rezin king of Aram to death.
When Ahaz went to Damascus, he saw an altar there and sent its design and plans to Uriah the priest so that he would build a similar altar in Jerusalem.
Ahaz ordered the bronze altar that stood before the LORD to be moved and placed beside the new altar, to its north.
After Ahaz died, he was buried in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah succeeded him as king.
